newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares down but end off lows after Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares down but end off lows after Ciampi.

text.p: Italian shares, weak all day, reduced losses in late trading on Tuesday after Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi slammed French President Jacques Chirac over his remarks doubting Italy would be among the first joining a single European currency, traders said.
Chirac later appeared to make a U-turn saying he hoped in fact Italy would make it but the two-way row buffeted the bond market and at one point put this week's Franco-Italian summit in doubt.
However, traders said the polemics had a limited effect on the stock market where trading was mainly technical and dominated by professionals.
The all-share Mibtel index ended down 1.0 pct and the Mib30 blue chip index closed off 1.13 pct.
The Mibtel index closed at 10,074 after a range of 10,034 and 10,110. The Mib30 index ended at 15,172 after a high at 15,241 and low of 15,109.
Volume was estimated as low, around 615 billion lire against Monday's 764 billion lire.
Wall Street's slight recovery after NAPM data helped sentiment somewhat, traders said.

Olivetti, after announcing late Monday its debts almost doubled during July and August, fell 6.48 percent to 525 lire. Eni was 1.5 percent off at 7,685 and Fiat down 1.56 percent at 4,220. Telecoms and banks were all weak.
